fix_commit_message:
[regexp] Fix OOB read in RegExpMatchGlobalAtom_OneCharPattern

We were loading (just not accessing) a character potentially beyond
the allocated string subject buffer.

Fixed: 439758498
Change-Id: I250670122c765640602b20e6640d604c9d33be03
Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/v8/v8/+/6871496

agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 5666bca708c0 on top of intro 36f07e9a0448 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (OutOfBoundsRead): RegExpMatchGlobalAtom_OneCharPattern in V8's regexp runtime uses SIMD (via Highway) to scan a subject string for occurrences of a single-character atom pattern, processing the bulk of the string in vector-width blocks and then falling back to a scalar loop for any trailing characters that don't fill a full SIMD lane. The scalar tail loop was written as `for (SChar c = *block; block < end; c = *(++block))`, which unconditionally reads `*block` in the for-loop initializer before the `block < end` bound check is performed. When the SIMD loops consume the subject string exactly to its end (leaving zero remaining scalar characters), `block` already equals `end`, and this initializer read accesses one character past the end of the allocated string buffer -- an out-of-bounds read. Root cause: The scalar cleanup loop's for-statement puts a pointer dereference in the initializer clause, which is unconditionally evaluated once before the loop's controlling condition is checked. This violates the invariant that `block` must be checked against `end` before every dereference, allowing a read exactly at (one past) the end of the subject string's backing buffer when there are no trailing characters left to scan.
